unspecified_scores.reason: Confirmed at PdfPagesPanel.tsx:139-151: `half` is taken from the scroller rect once per observer creation (deps `[firstRatio, state.numPages]`), so resizing the browser window or changing the phone sheet's height leaves the pre-draw margin sized for the old height, and the user only sees thumbnails start drawing slightly earlier or later than intended; the cells inside the visible box are still drawn.

Confirmed at PdfPagesPanel.tsx:198 and :319: the cap counts only `drawn`, and every `entered` (drawing) cell mounts a `<Page>`, so quickly flinging through a 200+ page PDF can start a render of nearly every page before eviction trims `drawn` back to 120; the user sees at most a brief CPU and memory spike from small 128px canvases, and nothing is displayed wrongly.

specification_compliance: There were no findings to verify. I read PdfPagesPanel.tsx at the reviewed state to score the two unspecified behaviors.

I3 cap: the eviction runs in a useEffect (PdfPagesPanel.tsx:197-219) after `drawn` grows, so for one committed render `drawn.size` can be 121 before the trim. The trim brings it back to 120, and nothing a user can see depends on that one frame.
I5: a cell's onClick (PdfPagesPanel.tsx:326) is the only goToPage call in the rail. The following effect (161-195) writes only `root.scrollTop`, which is consistent.

potential_unspecified_behavior.behavior: A cell in `drawing` that is scrolled far away before its render finishes is not cancelled. It stays in `entered` and keeps its `<Page>` mounted until the render finishes, and only then becomes eligible for eviction (PdfPagesPanel.tsx:216-218 evicts only members of `drawn`).
potential_unspecified_behavior.reason: Fast scrolling through a long PDF finishes renders for pages that are already off screen, which costs some background work and nothing visible.

regression_risks: The IntersectionObserver margin is fixed when the observer is created. Layout changes after that (window resize, sheet height) change how much is pre-drawn but do not stop visible cells from drawing.
test_coverage: I did not read the unit or e2e tests, because there were no findings to reproduce. The scores rest only on reading the component.
not_verified: I did not run the code. Every behavior was judged by reading PdfPagesPanel.tsx alone.
I did not check whether the phone sheet can change height while mounted (MobileInspectorSheet.tsx not read), which affects how often entry 0 triggers.
I did not measure the peak number of concurrent `<Page>` renders during a fast scroll.
